title: Heterogeneity in meta-analysis in the browser: a tool validated against the R package metafor
description: Archive v1.1.0 (2026-10-22) validates the original heterogeneity validation for the byte-exact allmeta v1.8.0 app at commit 1cb3f8409c7af75ed41f7e1811f9c502f900fc79 (release DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23515177; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20516880). New in this archive: the updated app and recursively required assets, portable Windows run plan, SHA-256 inventories, and display-card lookups adapted to the current labels. The original corpus, reference R code, expected values, and numerical tolerances are unchanged: metafor 5.2-1 with metadat 1.6-0; 88 meta-analyses, 49 datasets, 2,241 study rows, eight estimators, 704 configurations, and an expected 131,781 numerical checks plus 120,720 original displayed-number checks. The final 2026-10-22 release run passed (RUN_EXIT 0). Quick: 4934/4934 numerical, 4480/4480 display, 11/11 expected values. Full: 131781/131781 numerical, 120720/120720 display, 44/44 expected values. Display failures: 0 in both modes; no expected count differs. R 4.6.0 (metafor 5.2.1, metadat 1.6.0), Node 24.16.0 (Playwright 1.59.1), Python 3.13.13, Windows AMD64; Chromium 148.0.7778.96. Tool-version deviations were permitted with --allow-version-mismatch and are recorded in RECUT_NOTES.md and provenance/run_plan-2026-10-22-release.log; desktop R/metafor/metadat pins were enforced. This records a Windows runner pass, not a new canonical Docker or cross-platform pass. APP.txt specifies no numerical plus suite for heterogeneity (PR #163: strict numeric input usability). The optional in-page stored-reference replay and live webR dependency bundle are included as app assets; the bundled webR metafor 4.8-0 is distinct from the desktop validation reference metafor 5.2-1. Includes the corpus builder, original reference and analysis scripts, historical paper artifacts, Docker setup, and CI configuration. The earlier v1.0.0 validation targeted allmeta commit 7cb5975429531791d1879e80cf5c05f765e82c21 (PR #82).
